geography.notes: Limited to Lakeland Electric commercial customers on eligible GSLD, Interruptible, or ELDC rates.

hardRequirements: Must be a GSLD, Interruptible, or ELDC Lakeland Electric customer.
Energy audit by Lakeland Electric or a qualified engineering or energy services provider is required before work begins.
Account Executive must approve the energy-saving measures before rebate processing.
Invoice and post-installation verification are required.
Limit one rebate per customer; rebates depend on approval and fund availability.
blockers: Standalone energy audits are not the incentivized measure; the audit is a prerequisite.
Residential and small general-service customers are outside the stated eligible rates.
Measures outside lighting, HVAC, and motors require case-by-case approval.
repairs.evidenceText: Lakeland Electric states the rebate is $150 per kW demand reduction for eligible energy conservation measures, specifically lighting systems, HVAC, and motors, after a required energy audit.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Targets came from the uploaded repair queue . The prior energy_audit match should be blocked as a standalone retrofit because the audit is only a prerequisite for physical conservation measures.

geography.notes: Projects must be at Commonwealth/state facilities in Massachusetts.

hardRequirements: Applicant must be an eligible Massachusetts state entity.
Project must restore, repair, or replace existing state-owned solar PV or decarbonized systems at state facilities.
Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until June 30, 2027, or until funding is exhausted.
Per-site grants are capped by the program opportunity notice.
blockers: Not for private, residential, municipal, or commercial applicants.
New solar deployment belongs to the separate LBE Solar-Decarbonization Grant Program unless the project restores an existing system.
Do not generalize to generic rooftop solar where the source only supports existing system restoration.
repairs.evidenceText: COMMBUYS lists the LBE Restoration Grant Program for Solar and Decarbonized Systems as an open DOER grant opportunity with a June 30, 2027 bid opening date.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Solar PV is supported, but the opportunity is narrower than generic rooftop solar: it funds restoration of existing state-owned solar PV and decarbonized systems.

geography.notes: Only privately owned properties in Michigan jurisdictions that have joined the Lean and Green Michigan PACE program are eligible.

hardRequirements: Property must be privately owned and located in a participating Michigan PACE jurisdiction.
Eligible property generally includes commercial, industrial, agricultural, nonprofit, and multifamily properties with at least four units.
A baseline energy audit or approved assessment is required.
Mortgage-lender consent and program approval are required.
Financing terms and project economics must satisfy Lean and Green Michigan program rules.
blockers: Standalone energy audits are due-diligence requirements, not the primary retrofit incentive.
Single-family residential property is not an eligible PACE property under the program manual.
Do not treat this as a rebate; it is PACE financing repaid through an assessment.
repairs.evidenceText: The program manual defines PACE financing for privately owned eligible properties in member jurisdictions, covering energy efficiency, water efficiency, and renewable energy systems, with required audits and mortgage consent.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The energy_audit match is a false positive for retrofit matching. The source supports financing for qualifying improvements, while audits are required documentation.

geography.notes: Statewide Texas program when open.

hardRequirements: Program page currently states the program is closed.
When open, vehicle must be a new light-duty vehicle with gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 pounds or less.
Vehicle must operate on CNG, LPG, hydrogen fuel cell, plug-in electric, or plug-in hybrid drive, or use an eligible CNG or LPG conversion system.
Applicant must title and register the vehicle in Texas and submit required purchase, lease, title, tax, and identity documents.
blockers: Not a building retrofit program.
Fuel cell match is only for hydrogen fuel cell vehicles, not stationary fuel cell systems.
No EV charger or fueling infrastructure is funded by this opportunity.
Applications cannot be matched as available while the program page says currently closed.
repairs.evidenceText: TCEQ’s LDPLIP page says the program is currently closed and, when open, covers new light-duty alternative-fuel vehicles or CNG/LPG conversion systems titled in Texas.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The supplied fuel_cell_system match must be repaired to vehicle-specific hydrogen fuel cell purchase or lease. A stationary fuel cell building retrofit should be blocked.

geography.notes: Statewide New Jersey program for eligible public and nonprofit entities.

hardRequirements: Applicant must be one of the eligible public or 501(c)(3) nonprofit entity types.
Program provides no-cost energy audits, not automatic retrofit funding.
Audit participation and next steps are handled through NJ Clean Energy Program processes.
blockers: Not for residential households or private for-profit commercial customers.
Physical retrofit incentives are separate from the audit unless a separate NJCEP funding path applies.
Do not infer commercial equipment or weatherization measures from the audit program alone.
repairs.evidenceText: NJCEP states LGEA offers no-cost energy audits to local and state agencies, K-12 public schools, public agencies, state colleges and universities, and 501(c)(3) nonprofits.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The energy_audit match is supported. Keep it narrow because implementation incentives and funded retrofit projects are separate downstream opportunities.

geography.notes: Wyoming local governments; new audit intake is annual and time-limited.

hardRequirements: Local governments interested in the retrofit grant must first complete the WYLite Energy Audit.
WYLite Energy Audit applications are accepted March 1 through May 31 each year.
Retrofit grant maximum is $50,000 and requires a 10% match.
Retrofits must be one of the approved energy-efficiency categories.
blockers: New audit applications are outside the current annual application window as of July 2, 2026.
Not a residential or private commercial program.
Measures outside the listed approved retrofit categories are not source-backed.
repairs.evidenceText: Wyoming Energy Authority states WYLite audits are required before local government retrofit grants, with audit applications accepted March 1 to May 31 and approved retrofits listed.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The energy_audit match is valid only as the required WYLite audit path; the grant also supports specific physical efficiency retrofits.

geography.notes: Only commercial properties in Oklahoma counties that participate in the Oklahoma C-PACE program.

hardRequirements: Property must be an eligible commercial property in a participating county.
Qualifying improvements must be permanently affixed.
Project must satisfy Oklahoma C-PACE program guidelines and professional certification requirements.
Written mortgage-holder consent is required when applicable.
Property owner must be current on required obligations.
blockers: Standalone energy audits are not the financing purpose; they are project documentation or due diligence.
Public property, single-family residential, and residential-zoned property are not eligible under program guidelines.
Do not treat C-PACE financing as a rebate.
repairs.evidenceText: Oklahoma C-PACE is commercial property assessed clean energy financing for building owners, with program guidelines covering energy efficiency, renewable energy, water, and resilience improvements.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The prior energy_audit match should be blocked for standalone matching. Eligible categories should reflect financed qualifying improvements.

geography.notes: Local option program; municipalities must adopt an energy efficiency and clean energy district before projects can proceed.

hardRequirements: Municipality must adopt the C-PACER chapter and establish a district.
Eligible property excludes residential property with fewer than five dwelling units.
Improvements generally must be permanently affixed to the commercial property.
Program administrator approval, qualified analysis or engineering study, and mortgagee consent are required where applicable.
Repayment term may not exceed statutory limits.
blockers: Standalone energy audits are not the incentive; analyses and studies are project requirements or financeable ancillary costs.
Single-family homes and small residential properties under five units are excluded.
Local adoption is required before a property can use the financing.
repairs.administrator: New Hampshire Business Finance Authority and participating municipalities
repairs.evidenceText: New Hampshire law defines C-PACER qualifying improvements to include energy efficiency, clean energy, water conservation, and resiliency improvements, with local district adoption and property eligibility limits.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The energy_audit term is not a standalone retrofit category. It should be represented only as a required analysis or possible ancillary finance cost.

geography.notes: Local option bond authority for Arkansas local governments.

hardRequirements: Local government must issue or authorize project bonds under the Arkansas local option authority.
Project must qualify as an energy efficiency project that reduces energy consumption or operational costs, or installs energy efficiency systems.
Financing terms, liens, and bond procedures must follow applicable local bond statutes and ordinances.
blockers: Not a direct rebate or grant to private property owners.
Standalone audits are not the bond-funded retrofit category unless included in an approved energy efficiency project.
Specific technologies are not source-backed beyond qualifying energy efficiency projects and systems.
repairs.administrator: Arkansas Energy Office and local governments
repairs.evidenceText: Arkansas state energy resources identify local government energy efficiency project bond authority tied to performance contracting and guaranteed energy savings projects.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The source supports bond financing for local-government energy efficiency projects, not a discrete energy_audit retrofit match. Confidence is medium because the current state page is high-level.

geography.notes: Only cities, towns, regional governmental entities, or counties that establish an Energy Revolving Loan Fund can offer loans.

hardRequirements: A city or town must establish the fund by ordinance or by-law after a public hearing.
Loan must finance or refinance energy conservation or renewable energy projects on privately held real property.
No loan may be made unless an energy audit was conducted on or after July 2, 2008.
Any administrator-established energy conservation measures for participation must be implemented.
Loan agreement is recorded as a betterment assessment.
blockers: No statewide automatic loan; local adoption and fund availability are required.
Energy audit is a prerequisite, not the funded retrofit category.
Do not classify this as a rebate or grant.
repairs.administrator: Locally administered by Massachusetts cities, towns, regional entities, or counties
repairs.evidenceText: Massachusetts law allows local Energy Revolving Loan Funds for privately held real property energy conservation and renewable energy projects, with an energy audit required before loans.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Repair removes standalone energy_audit as the opportunity match. The program is local financing for conservation and renewable projects.

geography.notes: Local option; a county, city, or town must adopt an ordinance setting the tax treatment.

hardRequirements: Local governing body must adopt the separate tax classification by ordinance.
Building must exceed Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code energy efficiency standards by 30% or meet an approved rating system.
Certification must be made by a qualified architect, engineer, licensed contractor, program certification, or local designee.
Tax rate on qualifying buildings cannot exceed the general real property tax rate.
blockers: Not a measure-level rebate for LEED-related work.
Land value is not part of the separate energy-efficient building classification.
Local adoption and certification are required.
repairs.evidenceText: Virginia law allows localities to tax energy-efficient buildings separately when they exceed code by 30% or meet Green Globes, LEED, EarthCraft, or ENERGY STAR home standards.
repairs.reasoningNotes: LEED certification is valid but too narrow alone. Matching should include equivalent green building and above-code certification categories.

geography.notes: Local option; Baltimore City, counties, or municipal corporations may adopt credits and set local criteria.

hardRequirements: Local government must grant the credit by law.
Building must qualify as a high performance building under Maryland Tax-Property § 9-242.
High performance building generally requires at least LEED Silver, residential NGBS Silver, a comparable rating, or state-approved comparable standards.
Local law determines credit amount, duration, criteria, and qualifications.
blockers: Not a statewide automatic tax credit.
Not a measure-level retrofit incentive.
LEED-only matching is incomplete because equivalent rating systems and NGBS Silver are also supported.
repairs.evidenceText: Maryland law allows local property tax credits for high performance buildings meeting LEED Silver, residential NGBS Silver, comparable ratings, or approved comparable standards.
repairs.reasoningNotes: LEED certification remains supported, but eligible categories must include equivalent high-performance building certifications and local-option blockers.

geography.notes: Local option; Baltimore City, counties, or municipal corporations must adopt the credit and define eligible devices.

hardRequirements: Local government must grant the property tax credit by law.
Device must be used to heat or cool the structure, generate electricity for use in the structure, or provide hot water for use in the structure.
Eligible device must be a solar energy device, geothermal energy device, or qualifying energy conservation device as defined locally.
Local law sets credit amount and duration; duration may not exceed three years.
blockers: Not a statewide automatic tax credit.
Local governments define solar, geothermal, and qualifying energy conservation devices.
Do not match generic geothermal projects unless the device serves the structure as required.
repairs.evidenceText: Maryland law authorizes local property tax credits for structures using solar energy devices, geothermal energy devices, or qualifying energy conservation devices.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The geothermal heat pump match is source-supported but must remain device-specific and subject to local definitions and adoption.

geography.notes: Local option exemption; county, city, town, village, or school district must adopt it.

hardRequirements: Local taxing jurisdiction or school district must adopt the exemption.
Construction or reconstruction must commence on or after the local qualifying date.
Property must be owned by an individual or private organization.
Project must meet LEED, Green Globes, ANSI national green building standards, or a substantially equivalent local standard.
Project value must exceed $10,000 and cannot be ordinary maintenance or repairs.
blockers: Not available where the local taxing jurisdiction has not opted in.
Ordinary maintenance and repairs are not eligible.
Not a rebate for isolated LEED-related products or documentation only.
repairs.administrator: New York local taxing jurisdictions and school districts
repairs.evidenceText: New York’s tax manual describes a local-option partial exemption for certified green building construction or reconstruction meeting LEED, Green Globes, ANSI, or equivalent standards.
repairs.reasoningNotes: LEED is supported but should be matched as one of several green building certification pathways, with local-option and construction-value requirements.

geography.notes: Limited to Lodi Electric Utility commercial and industrial customers on specified electric rates.

hardRequirements: Customer must be on G1, G2, G3, G4, G5, or I1 electric utility rate.
Customer must be current on utility charges with no late charges for the prior 18 months.
Customer must have an active City of Lodi account for the prior 18 months.
Project must receive a rebate through the City of Lodi Electric Utility Public Benefits/Energy Efficiency Program.
Customer must submit an energy efficiency audit or contractor proposal; minimum post-rebate project cost is $1,500.
blockers: Standalone energy audits are application documentation, not the financed retrofit category.
Residential customers outside eligible commercial/industrial rates are not eligible.
Loan is on-bill 0% financing, not a rebate-only program.
repairs.evidenceText: Lodi Electric Utility offers on-bill zero-percent financing for commercial and industrial energy efficient improvements such as LED lighting, HVAC, manufacturing equipment, and refrigeration.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The energy_audit term is a requirement to submit an audit or contractor proposal. Matching should use the financed physical efficiency measures and financing category.

geography.notes: Limited to qualifying LG&E and KU residential electric and small business customers.

hardRequirements: Customer must be a qualifying LG&E or KU residential or small business electric customer.
Customer must have an eligible internet-connected smart thermostat connected to central air conditioning.
Customer must allow brief thermostat adjustments during high-demand periods.
Customer cannot also be enrolled in the LG&E and KU Demand Conservation program.
Thermostat model must be on the approved list.
blockers: Not a general HVAC zoning retrofit program.
Incentive is for enrolling an eligible smart thermostat in demand response, not for broad HVAC equipment replacement.
Customers already enrolled in the conflicting demand conservation program must unenroll before enrolling.
repairs.administrator: Louisville Gas and Electric and Kentucky Utilities
repairs.evidenceText: The FAQ says qualifying LG&E and KU residential electric and small business customers with eligible smart thermostats receive enrollment and event incentives for thermostat adjustments.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The thermostat match is supported, but it should be narrowed to smart thermostat demand response rather than general HVAC zoning.

geography.notes: Limited to eligible LG&E and KU small business account holders on listed rates.

hardRequirements: Customer must have an active LG&E or KU account with service under eligible General Service electric options or LG&E CGS or IGS rate options.
Customer must own or operate a qualifying small business.
Services may not be provided under this program more than once in a three-year period.
Customer must enroll through the utility process and provide required account and tax information.
blockers: Not a residential program.
Business Rebates is a separate program for additional incentives.
Do not infer specific equipment categories beyond basic direct-install energy-efficient equipment unless the utility specifies measures for the site.
repairs.administrator: Louisville Gas and Electric and Kentucky Utilities
repairs.evidenceText: LG&E and KU state the program provides an energy audit and basic energy-efficient equipment at no additional cost to eligible small business customers.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The energy_audit match is supported and should be paired with direct_install_energy_efficiency, while downstream Business Rebates must remain separate.

geography.notes: Federal block grant administered by states, territories, tribes, and local agencies; benefits and application windows vary by grantee.

hardRequirements: Household must meet the applicable state, territory, tribal, or local LIHEAP eligibility rules.
Assistance is administered by local LIHEAP grantees, not directly as a universal federal retrofit rebate.
Weatherization and minor energy-related repairs depend on local grantee program options and funding.
Funding is limited and may be seasonal.
blockers: Not a commercial or institutional retrofit program.
Weatherization is optional and locally administered; do not assume every LIHEAP application funds physical retrofit work.
LIHEAP should not be matched as a building retrofit rebate where the local grantee only provides bill or crisis assistance.
repairs.administrator: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Administration for Children and Families, Office of Community Services
repairs.evidenceText: ACF describes LIHEAP as federally funded assistance for home energy bills, energy crises, weatherization, and minor energy-related home repairs for low-income households.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The weatherization match is conditionally valid but must be flagged as locally administered and not universal across all LIHEAP grantees.

geography.notes: Statewide Delaware program regardless of electric utility service territory.

hardRequirements: Low-income households must apply through the Weatherization Assistance Program and meet WAP income eligibility.
Low-income qualified homes may receive cost-free solar up to 4.0 kW.
Moderate-income households apply through approved solar contractors and must meet state area median income limits.
Moderate-income qualified households receive 70% program payment and 30% homeowner payment for systems up to 6.0 kW.
Income is verified through tax returns and required household forms.
blockers: Weatherization itself is a separate prerequisite pathway, not the solar pilot’s funded retrofit category.
Not available to commercial, industrial, or nonresidential applicants.
Do not match as general air sealing or weatherization; this opportunity is for residential solar installation.
repairs.administrator: Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control
repairs.evidenceText: DNREC states the LMI Solar Pilot provides cost-free or reduced-cost solar installations for low- and moderate-income Delaware households, with low-income applications through Weatherization.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The supplied weatherization match is a false positive for the funded opportunity. Weatherization is a separate pathway or prerequisite for low-income eligibility.

geography.notes: Limited to MGE residential electric customers charging an EV at the registered home address.

hardRequirements: Customer must be an MGE residential electric customer who owns or leases an EV and charges at home.
Customer must connect a compatible EV or compatible home charger through the ev.energy app.
Smart charging must remain enabled to earn standard-rate customer rewards.
Standard-rate customers must charge at least 80% off-peak and have no more than three unmanaged sessions in a month to earn monthly rewards.
MGE only manages charging at the registered home address.
blockers: Not an EV charger installation rebate.
Public and workplace charging are not managed by the program.
A separate MGE EV charging rebate effort, if approved, should not be merged into Charge Ahead.
repairs.evidenceText: MGE Charge Ahead lets residential EV customers earn rewards by connecting a compatible EV or charger and smart charging at home during off-peak periods.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The prior ev_charger_installation match is a false positive. The source supports managed charging behavior and performance rewards, not charger purchase or installation.
